clue.text: President's in la-la land! Go — and quickly!

indicators.note: the president's name is placed inside the letters for la-la land

parts.note: La-la Land is a nickname for Los Angeles, LA
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
a go at something is a shot at it

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry telling a dreaming president to get moving at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the insertion signal; 'la-la land' is a nickname for Los Angeles, not a fantasy world.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doing something immediately and eagerly is a synonym for quickly.

clue.text: Allowed American tax evader to take stage first

indicators.note: the gangster's name takes the stage word before it, so they join as a pair
the stage word comes first, ahead of the gangster's name

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, was finally jailed for tax evasion

explanation.surface: A famous American tax dodger is allowed to go onstage first.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Capone was convicted of tax evasion rather than his other crimes, so the clue points to his first name AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law is lawful, so allowed is a synonym.

clue.text: Liberal take on MP entertaining with mistress

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the jumbled letters hold the abbreviation for with
a liberal version is a free one, so the letters are rearranged loosely

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician's view of an MP who is carrying on with a mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like a party label but signals the anagram of TAKEONMP; 'entertaining' then puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman financially supported by a lover in return for an affair is a traditional sense of mistress.

clue.text: Surprised at bone spurs (nothing cut out) — that's being rude!

indicators.note: surprised letters are startled out of place, so they are rearranged
to cut out something is to remove it, so the round letter goes from the fodder

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone startled by a doctor's finding of bone spurs, then scolded for being impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing cut out' takes O from ATBONESPURS, and 'Surprised' rearranges the remaining ATBNESPURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtness of manner is a kind of rudeness, so the quality of being rude fits the noun.

clue.text: Men getting brown stopping in sun

indicators.note: the brown abbreviation stops up the word for in, sitting inside it

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
BR is a short form of brown
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Men getting a tan by staying out in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a piece, not a link: being in means being at HOME, which BR then stops up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is Spanish for man, used in English slang for a fellow or guy.

clue.text: Laugh about Washington's leader — what's he on?

indicators.note: the laugh goes round the leading letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a titter is a nervous little laugh

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of Washington is used

explanation.surface: A mocking laugh at a Washington leader, wondering what drug he is on.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue dates from Donald Trump's presidency; 'what's he on?' sounds like a question about drugs but asks which platform he posts on.
explanation.definitionFit: The social media platform was the president's favoured channel for posting messages at the time.

clue.text: She's suffering daily

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A woman who endures hardship every single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: the answer is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name is a fair answer to the pronoun for any female person.

clue.text: Slow learner gets letter wrong way round

parts.note: L is for learner, as on L-plates for learner drivers

indicators.note: turned the wrong way round, the Greek letter reads backwards

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A slow pupil keeps writing a letter back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' means a Greek letter here, and 'wrong way round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock or watch that is behind the correct time is said to be slow.

clue.text: Spin a lot of rubbish

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: drivel is silly nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Political spin dismissed as largely rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' sounds like media spin, but it means a ride out in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure trip in a car, the same as a drive.

clue.text: Tricks boy's acquired — they're inflammatory!

indicators.note: the trickery word takes in the boy's words, holding them inside

parts.note: arts are wiles or cunning tricks
a boy is a son, and the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: A boy has picked up some tricks that are bound to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boy's' gives SON IS, the 's read as is, placed inside ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-raisers are literally inflammatory, playing on the word's usual sense of stirring up trouble.

clue.text: Greek primate's eaten shellfish

indicators.note: the primate has been eaten, so it sits inside the Greek abbreviation

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A Greek monkey has gobbled up some shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the ape doing the eating, but 'eaten' means the primate is swallowed by the Greek abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The gaper is a large edible clam, a burrowing bivalve mollusc.

clue.text: Insists chief isn't a criminal

parts.note: chief and main both mean principal

indicators.note: a criminal is crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insisting their boss is not a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like part of the story but is the anagram signal for 'isn't a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep asserting something firmly is to insist on it.

clue.text: See women planning trips with kids. occasionally — one's down with them

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: planning is arranging, so these letters are put in a fresh order
occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of kids is taken

explanation.surface: Mothers organising trips with the children, now and then feeling glum about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes IS from kids; 'planning' rearranges TRIPS with IS. 'one's down with them' means depressed while in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a gloomy, dejected mood is down, which the phrase for depression describes.

clue.text: Annoyance to the royals? That's heartless and unkind

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its two central letters

parts.note: Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, whose departure from royal duties was seen as a headache for the British royal family

explanation.surface: Something that irritates the royal family is said to be cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared just after Prince Harry and Meghan stepped back from royal duties in 2020; the question mark flags that she is a jokey definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nasty or spiteful towards others is a common synonym of unkind.

clue.text: Enjoying a good relationship? First Lady's reticent at first — I wasn't expecting that …

parts.note: to be well in with someone is to be on good terms with them
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of reticent is used

explanation.surface: A US First Lady, reserved at first, is surprised to be getting on well with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife but means EVE, the first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of astonishment says the same as admitting surprise at an unexpected turn.

clue.text: Maine bankers invested in US money and bonds

indicators.note: the picked letters are put into the money, sitting inside it

parts.note: cents are small units of American money

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its edges, so the outside letters of Maine are taken

explanation.surface: Bankers in the state of Maine putting dollars into financial bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bankers' looks like financiers but means the banks, or edges, of Maine; 'invested in' puts them inside the money.
explanation.definitionFit: To bond things is to stick them together, which a builder's glue or mortar does.

clue.text: … mind you, she does say Vlad's right about Republican at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, being at the top means coming first, so these lead

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
EG, for example, is what say means here
Vlad is the setter, so Vlad's means I have, shortened to I've

explanation.surface: The setter carries on from the clue before, claiming she would vouch for his politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 13 down's ellipsis; the setter's name stands for 'I', so 'Vlad's' gives I'VE, and 'say' gives EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after somebody, minding them, which is exactly the job described.

clue.text: Conserving energy, passes on the wacky baccy

definitions.note: a singular phrase for cannabis, standing for the plural joints of it

indicators.note: conserving means keeping something inside, so the letter for energy is held within

parts.note: to refer a matter is to pass it on to someone else
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An energy-saving smoker hands round some cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passes on' looks like declining, but it means REFERS, which holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis cigarettes are joints, a slang term for marijuana smoked in a roll-up.

clue.text: Game is on TV — fee to be arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A sports match is to be televised once the broadcast fee is agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON FIVES is a handball game played in a walled court, devised at Eton College, an English private school.
explanation.definitionFit: A handball game played against walls is a sport, which game covers.

clue.text: Mentions bishop's missed calls

indicators.note: the bishop is missed, meaning absent, so that letter goes

parts.note: to bring up a subject is to mention it
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a bishop failed to answer phone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed calls' reads as phone jargon, but 'missed' acts on bishop and 'calls' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone on the telephone is to call them.

clue.text: Experts, quiet ones, impress department

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the department letter goes inside the ones

parts.note: units are ones, single things

explanation.surface: Quiet specialists who manage to impress their department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' looks like awe but means press in: D goes into UNITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Pundits are authorities who comment on a subject, so they are experts.

clue.text: Artist carrying can shouts at pack

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the painter holds the toilet

parts.note: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age portrait painter
can is slang for a toilet, as is loo

explanation.surface: A painter holding a tin yells at a pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is slang for a lavatory, LOO, not a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunters cry halloo to urge on the hounds, so the verb means calling out to them.

clue.text: Shelter to put up poor person

parts.note: a haven is a refuge or shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up reads it upwards, so it is backwards

explanation.surface: A shelter offered to house a person in poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like giving lodging but reverses 'to' into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are the poor, people lacking money or possessions.

clue.text: Shallow and largely fake — bigly!

indicators.note: a fake version is not genuine, so the letters are reworked
largely means mostly, so the final letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A jibe at a politician's shallow, phony boast that something is huge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bigly' was Donald Trump's notorious word; 'largely' trims its Y and 'fake' scrambles BIGL.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib remark is superficial and slick, lacking depth or thought.

clue.text: Moved furtively heading off, but didn't do anything

indicators.note: with the heading off, the first letter is removed

parts.note: to sidle is to edge along stealthily

explanation.surface: Someone crept away sneakily but achieved nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to laze about without doing work.

clue.text: Odd — square in the centre awfully quiet

parts.note: odd things are not matching, uneven
a T-square is a draughtsman's tool, so T can stand for square

indicators.note: only the central letters of awfully are used, the three in its middle

explanation.surface: Something oddly calm in the middle of a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the centre' takes FUL, the middle three letters of awfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiet day is one in which nothing notable happens.

clue.text: Charges youngsters over ecstasy

indicators.note: the youngsters cover over the drug letter, holding it among them

parts.note: lads are young boys
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Young people charged with drug offences over ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' sounds legal but means loads, as a ship lades cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: To lade is to load cargo, so to load or burden is what the verb means.

clue.text: Picked up passenger OK

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: a fare is a paying passenger in a taxi

explanation.surface: A cabbie collects a passenger and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' plays on a taxi collecting a fare.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means reasonable or acceptable, middling but adequate.

clue.text: Valuing mostly art? Unlikely — he's got money but no taste

definitions.text: he's got money but no taste

indicators.note: unlikely suggests the letters are out of their probable order
mostly means most of the word, so the final letter is cut

explanation.surface: Doubting that a rich man values art, given his lack of taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims art to AR, and 'Unlikely' shuffles VALUINGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse, showy person with no refinement, often newly rich, is a crass individual.

clue.text: Very, very angry losing head — that's clear

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter goes

parts.note: livid means furious, very angry

explanation.surface: Someone extremely furious, then calming down, says that's quite clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Very' is V; the second goes with 'angry' to give LIVID.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid picture is sharp and distinct, plain to see.

clue.text: Thoroughbred irritated over what it's carrying

definitions.text: Thoroughbred irritated over what it's carrying

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the hidden letters read backwards
the clue words carry the answer within them

explanation.surface: A racehorse annoyed by the jockey on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, thoroughbRED IRritated holds the answer; the whole clue also describes it, as an irritated horse carries a jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse carries a jockey, the person astride it.

clue.text: Times empty on day — Murdoch's writers taking the mick

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
Iris Murdoch was a British novelist

indicators.note: an empty word loses its contents, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: Rupert Murdoch's Times hacks mocking people on a quiet day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch' suggests Rupert, owner of The Times, but is novelist Iris Murdoch. 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: People who use humour and ridicule to mock others are mockers.
